content.comment_body: Hello everyone, Is it possible to change date format from English (YY-MM-DD) to French (DD-MM-YY)? And can the days of the week be displayed in French instead of English abbreviations (MTWTFSS to LMMJVSD)? My clients mostly don't speak English and get confused with the weekly timer settings via the web interface, which only uses English formats.
Unfortunately, the interface supports only English.

Is there any method to display the format differently? Perhaps splitting memory usage and showing groupings as needed? Personally, I suggest leaving the format as is but including a note about date formatting (YY.MM.DD) to help users.

In my view, modifying this would be impractical and not advisable. The product manages date and time internally with BCD code, which would require conversion to decimal. The time and date can't be accessed except for display in message text or parameters. The VM storage area for time and date starts from VB 990 and is meant for communication with external devices, such as an operator panel. The VM storage accessible by user programs ranges from V0.0 to V850.7.
Thank you for sharing your perspective. After considering this further, I agree with your point.

analysis.insight_summary: Users require localized date and day formats in the device's web interface, especially for French language support. The current solution only displays English formats (YY-MM-DD, MTWTFSS), creating challenges for non-English users. Though alternatives like memory adjustments or adding formatting notes have been suggested, they are either impractical or serve only as partial solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate the web interface will allow dates and day names to be shown in French to better align with local requirements and help users avoid confusion.
